subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should permanent Gateway WebSocket hardening live in the existing HTTP upgrade handler with a narrowed configuration contract, or should OpenClaw adopt this separate ws verifyClient layer and three new settings?
rationale: The choice changes a network security boundary and public configuration surface; upstream discourages verifyClient, while current main already has a central pre-101 upgrade path, so maintainer intent is required before implementation details are finalized.

options.title: Use the existing upgrade boundary
options.body: Move the checks into attachGatewayUpgradeHandler, inspect raw headers there, and expose only the minimum explicitly approved opt-in policy.

options.title: Keep verifyClient
options.body: Approve the separate verifyClient layer, then require every rejection to be opt-in, fix raw-header handling, document the split boundary, and add live handshake proof.

options.title: Decline the new surface
options.body: Retain current post-connect origin enforcement and pursue only narrower hardening that does not add configuration or a second admission policy.

recommendation.title: Use the existing upgrade boundary
recommendation.body: Move the checks into attachGatewayUpgradeHandler, inspect raw headers there, and expose only the minimum explicitly approved opt-in policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor explicitly requested this person's call on the Gateway security boundary and configuration naming.
